newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 19.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister-designate Chavalit Yongchaiyudh moves to form Cabinet. Bouyed by his narrow victory over the Democrats, Chavalit moved swiftly yesterday in negotiations for the formation of his Cabinet by bringing in the Chart Pattana Party. In an apparent swtich, the New Aspiration leader excluded Banharn Silpa-archa's Chart Thai Party from the coalition.

Gen Chavalit called on Chatichai Choonhavan, the Chart Pattana leader, at his residence to discuss the formation of the new cabinet which will be derived from the NAP, Chart Pattana, Social Action, Prachakorn Thai, Muan Chon and Seritham. (BANGKOK POST)

- Police react to King's appeal for flood relief. His Masjesty the King instructed police to help provide emergency assistance to residents in three southern provinces as tropical storm Ernie approached the Thai coast, a police spokesman said.
The Royal instruction was given as the tropical storm approached the upper southern coast, triggering downpours over Chumphorn and other neighbouring provinces yesterday. (THE NATION).

- Share price dive a message for NAP. New Aspiration has narrowly won the right to form the government, but it has yet to win the hearts of investors and business people. Investors "voted" by sending the stock market tumbling 5.8 percent yesterday. It was not unexpected. Even before the election, the stock market took its cue from political trends. Whenever the number of incumbent MPs switching to New Aspiration increased, the stock market fell; and whenever the Democrats looked more likely to win, the market rose. (BANGKOK POST) - Chavalit given a cautious welcome. A potential lineup of eocnomic ministers has emerged for the new coalition government which will be led by New Aspiration Party leader General Chavalit Yongchaiyudh. The NAP-led coalition, with Chavalit as prime minister, is expected to name Amnauy Viravan, a respected former banker, as finance minister, while coalition member Chart Pattana Party will likely name Korn Dabaransi as industry minister, according to party sources. (THE NATION

- Thai Airways chief warns against delaying development plan. Any delay to the business development plan of Thai would result in damage to the company through a drop in earnings and an increase in operational costs, Thai president Thamnoon Wanglee said. The five-year plan of the national carrier is expected to be submitted to Cabinet today. (BUSINESS DAY)
